**1 — Scene:** A meal of roasted chicken, white rice, leafy salad with dark olives, and green beans.

**2 — Vessel:** A large, roughly square dinner plate, partly cropped. Using an equivalent circular diameter of about **28 cm** gives an area of **615 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Chicken with skin, cooked white rice, leafy greens, black olives, and green beans. The beans have a slight sheen; I estimate **3 g of oil**.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:** Estimates refer only to the visible portions.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| Roasted chicken with skin | 10% | 62 cm² × 1.8 cm = 112 ml | 0.95 → 106 g | 215 | 228 kcal |
| White rice | 18% | 111 cm² × 1.4 cm = 155 ml | 0.8 → 124 g | 130 | 161 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 24% | 148 cm² × 2 cm = 296 ml | 0.15 → 44 g | 25 | 11 kcal |
| Black olives | 1% | 6 cm² × 0.9 cm = 5 ml | 1.0 → 5 g | 115 | 6 kcal |
| Green beans | 8% | 49 cm² × 1.1 cm = 54 ml | 0.6 → 32 g | 35 | 11 kcal |
| Oil | On beans; no additional footprint | Approximately 3 ml | 0.9 → 3 g | 884 | 27 kcal |

**8 — Sanity check:** Food covers approximately **61%** of the plate, leaving a substantial empty area. The estimated total is **314 g and 444 kcal**, plausible for the visible modest rice mound, airy salad, small bean portion, and cropped chicken portion. Chicken weight and cooking oil are the largest uncertainties.
